presentation predicates coincide. -/
theorem isPolyhedron_iff_isPolyhedral {p : Set E} :
    IsPolyhedron p ↔ IsPolyhedral ℝ p

name: EulersGem.IsPolytope.isPolyhedron
statement:
/-- **Finite-vertex-to-finite-halfspace representation.** Every convex hull of
finitely many points is an intersection of finitely many closed halfspaces.
This includes empty and lower-dimensional polytopes. -/
theorem IsPolytope.isPolyhedron {p : Set E} (hp : IsPolytope p) : IsPolyhedron p

name: EulersGem.R3
statement:
/-- Real three-space. -/
abbrev R3 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

name: EulersGem.R3.crs
statement:
/-- Coordinate cross product. -/
noncomputable def crs (x y : R3) : R3 :=
  !₂[x 1 * y 2 - x 2 * y 1, x 2 * y 0 - x 0 * y 2, x 0 * y 1 - x 1 * y 0]

name: EulersGem.R3.crs_0
statement: @[simp] lemma crs_0 (x y : R3) : crs x y 0 = x 1 * y 2 - x 2 * y 1

name: EulersGem.R3.crs_1
statement: @[simp] lemma crs_1 (x y : R3) : crs x y 1 = x 2 * y 0 - x 0 * y 2

name: EulersGem.R3.crs_2
statement: @[simp] lemma crs_2 (x y : R3) : crs x y 2 = x 0 * y 1 - x 1 * y 0

name: EulersGem.R3.inner_eq
statement: lemma inner_eq (p q : R3) : ⟪p, q⟫ = p 0 * q 0 + p 1 * q 1 + p 2 * q 2

name: EulersGem.R3.toR3_cross
statement: lemma toR3_cross (u v : ZPhi.V) : (ZPhi.V.cross u v).toR3 = crs u.toR3 v.toR3

name: EulersGem.R3.inner_mul_crs
statement:
/-- A vector orthogonal to `x` and `y` is parallel to `x × y` (division-free form). -/
theorem inner_mul_crs {a x y : R3} (hx : ⟪a, x⟫ = 0) (hy : ⟪a, y⟫ = 0) (z : R3) :
    ⟪a, z⟫ * ⟪crs x y, crs x y⟫ = ⟪a, crs x y⟫ * ⟪crs x y, z⟫

name: EulersGem.R3.inner_self_crs_pos
statement: lemma inner_self_crs_pos {x y : R3} (h : crs x y ≠ 0) : 0 < ⟪crs x y, crs x y⟫

name: EulersGem.R3.linearIndependent_pair
statement:
/-- Two vectors with nonzero cross product are linearly independent. -/
theorem linearIndependent_pair {x y : R3} (h : crs x y ≠ 0) : LinearIndependent ℝ ![x, y]

name: EulersGem.R3.linearIndependent_triple
statement:
/-- Three vectors with nonzero triple product are linearly independent. -/
theorem linearIndependent_triple {x y z : R3} (h : ⟪crs x y, z⟫ ≠ 0) :
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![x, y, z]

name: EulersGem.R3.finrank_R3
statement: lemma finrank_R3 : Module.finrank ℝ R3 = 3

name: EulersGem.R3.affDim_eq_finrank_vectorSpan
statement:
lemma affDim_eq_finrank_vectorSpan {s : Set R3} (hs : s.Nonempty) :
    affDim s = (Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ s) : ℤ)

name: EulersGem.R3.affDim_convexHull
statement: lemma affDim_convexHull (s : Set R3) : affDim (convexHull ℝ s) = affDim s

name: EulersGem.R3.le_finrank_vectorSpan
statement:
/-- Lower bound on affine dimension from independent difference vectors. -/
lemma le_finrank_vectorSpan {s : Set R3} {k : ℕ} (v : Fin k → R3)
    (hv : LinearIndependent ℝ v) (hmem : ∀ i, v i ∈ vectorSpan ℝ s) :
    k ≤ Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ s)

name: EulersGem.R3.affDim_eq_two
statement:
/-- **A planar set spanned by a non-degenerate triangle has affine dimension 2.** -/
theorem affDim_eq_two {s : Set R3} {p q r : R3} (hp : p ∈ s) (hq : q ∈ s) (hr : r ∈ s)
    (hn : crs (q - p) (r - p) ≠ 0)
    (hplane : ∀ x ∈ s, ⟪crs (q - p) (r - p), x - p⟫ = 0) : affDim s = 2

name: EulersGem.R3.affDim_eq_three
statement:
/-- **Four points with nonzero triple product span all of three-space.** -/
theorem affDim_eq_three {s : Set R3} {p q r t : R3} (hp : p ∈ s) (hq : q ∈ s) (hr : r ∈ s)
    (ht : t ∈ s) (hn : ⟪crs (q - p) (r - p), t - p⟫ ≠ 0) : affDim s = 3

name: EulersGem.R3.affDim_pair
statement:
/-- A segment between distinct points has affine dimension 1. -/
theorem affDim_pair {p q : R3} (h : p ≠ q) : affDim ({p, q} : Set R3) = 1

name: EulersGem.vertexSet
statement:
/-- The vertices of `P`: points `x` such that `{x}` is a `0`-face. -/
def vertexSet (P : Set R3) : Set R3 := {x | {x} ∈ facesOfDim P 0}

name: EulersGem.vertexSet_finite
statement: lemma vertexSet_finite {P : Set R3} (hP : IsPolytope P) : (vertexSet P).Finite

name: EulersGem.image_vertexSet
statement:
lemma image_vertexSet {P : Set R3} {g : R3 ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] R3} (hg : g '' P = P) :
    g '' vertexSet P = vertexSet P

name: EulersGem.centroid_vertexSet_fixed
statement:
/-- A symmetry of `P` fixes the centroid of the vertices. -/
lemma centroid_vertexSet_fixed {P : Set R3} (hfin : (vertexSet P).Finite)
    (hne : hfin.toFinset.Nonempty) {g : R3 ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] R3} (hg : g '' P = P) :
    g (hfin.toFinset.centroid ℝ id) = hfin.toFinset.centroid ℝ id

name: EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron.exists_centre
statement:
/-- **A regular polyhedron has a centre.** Some point `c` (the centroid of the vertices) is
fixed by every symmetry of `P`, and all vertices of `P` are at the same distance `r` from
`c`. -/
theorem IsRegularPolyhedron.exists_centre {P : Set R3} (hP : IsRegularPolyhedron P)
    (hL : FaceLatticeFacts P) :
    ∃ c : R3, (∀ g : R3 ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] R3, g '' P = P → g c = c) ∧
      ∃ r : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ vertexSet P, dist x c = r

name: EulersGem.FaceLatticeFacts.edge_in_flag
statement:
/-- Every edge lies in a flag. -/
lemma FaceLatticeFacts.edge_in_flag {P : Set R3} (hP : IsPolytope P) (hL : FaceLatticeFacts P)
    {e : Set R3} (he : e ∈ facesOfDim P 1) : ∃ v f, IsFlag P v e f

name: EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron.edges_congruent'
statement:
/-- Any two edges of a regular polyhedron are exchanged by a symmetry. -/
theorem IsRegularPolyhedron.edges_congruent' {P : Set R3} (hP : IsRegularPolyhedron P)
    (hL : FaceLatticeFacts P) {e e' : Set R3} (he : e ∈ facesOfDim P 1)
    (he' : e' ∈ facesOfDim P 1) : ∃ g : R3 ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] R3, g '' P = P ∧ g '' e = e'

name: EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron.edges_congruent
statement:
/-- **All edges of a regular polyhedron have the same length** (`Metric.diam`, which for a
segment is its length). -/
theorem IsRegularPolyhedron.edges_congruent {P : Set R3} (hP : IsRegularPolyhedron P)
    (hL : FaceLatticeFacts P) :
    ∃ ℓ : ℝ, ∀ e ∈ facesOfDim P 1, Metric.diam e = ℓ

name: EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron.facets_congruent
statement:
/-- Any two facets of a regular polyhedron are exchanged by a symmetry. -/
theorem IsRegularPolyhedron.facets_congruent {P : Set R3} (hP : IsRegularPolyhedron P)
    (hL : FaceLatticeFacts P) {f f' : Set R3} (hf : f ∈ facesOfDim P 2)
    (hf' : f' ∈ facesOfDim P 2) : ∃ g : R3 ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] R3, g '' P = P ∧ g '' f = f'

name: EulersGem.FaceLatticeFacts
statement:
/-- Standard face-lattice facts of a convex 3-polytope that the repository does not yet
prove in general (general proof outstanding: `PlatonicGaps.GAP_faceLatticeFacts`).
They hold for the five constructed solids (`FaceLatticeFacts.of_faceData`,
`platonic_faceLatticeFacts`), so the hypothesis is not vacuous. -/
structure FaceLatticeFacts (P : Set R3) : Prop where
  exists_flag : ∃ v e f, IsFlag P v e f
  vertex_in_flag : ∀ v ∈ facesOfDim P 0, ∃ e f, IsFlag P v e f
  edge_in_facet : ∀ e ∈ facesOfDim P 1, ∃ f ∈ facesOfDim P 2, e ⊆ f
  facet_in_flag : ∀ f ∈ facesOfDim P 2, ∃ v e, IsFlag P v e f
  edge_two_facets : ∀ e ∈ facesOfDim P 1, {f ∈ facesOfDim P 2 | e ⊆ f}.ncard = 2
  facet_three_edges : ∀ f ∈ facesOfDim P 2, 3 ≤ {e ∈ facesOfDim P 1 | e ⊆ f}.ncard
  vertex_three_edges : ∀ v ∈ facesOfDim P 0, 3 ≤ {e ∈ facesOfDim P 1 | v ⊆ e}.ncard

name: EulersGem.nonempty_of_le_ncard
statement:
lemma nonempty_of_le_ncard {α : Type*} {s : Set α} {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (h : k ≤ s.ncard) :
    s.Nonempty

name: EulersGem.FaceLatticeFacts.of_faceData
statement:
/-- `FaceLatticeFacts` follows from `IsPolytope P` and the face data `{s, m}` with `s, m ≥ 3`
and at least one facet. -/
theorem FaceLatticeFacts.of_faceData {P : Set R3} (hP : IsPolytope P) {V E F s m : ℕ}
    (h : Platonic3.HasFaceData P V E F s m) (hs : 3 ≤ s) (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hF : 0 < F) :
    FaceLatticeFacts P

name: EulersGem.platonic_faceLatticeFacts
statement:
/-- The five constructed solids satisfy `FaceLatticeFacts` (non-vacuity of the hypothesis). -/
theorem platonic_faceLatticeFacts :
    FaceLatticeFacts Platonic3.tetrahedron ∧ FaceLatticeFacts Platonic3.cube ∧
    FaceLatticeFacts Platonic3.octahedron ∧ FaceLatticeFacts Platonic3.dodecahedron ∧
    FaceLatticeFacts Platonic3.icosahedron

name: EulersGem.image_mem_facesOfDim
statement:
lemma image_mem_facesOfDim (hg : g '' P = P) {F : Set R3} {d : ℤ}
    (hF : F ∈ facesOfDim P d) : g '' F ∈ facesOfDim P d

name: EulersGem.symm_image_eq
statement: lemma symm_image_eq (hg : g '' P = P) : g.symm '' P = P

name: EulersGem.image_symm_image
statement: lemma image_symm_image (s : Set R3) : g '' (g.symm '' s) = s

name: EulersGem.ncard_sub_image
statement:
/-- A symmetry preserves the number of `d`-faces inside a set. -/
lemma ncard_sub_image (hg : g '' P = P) (d : ℤ) (x : Set R3) :
    {y ∈ facesOfDim P d | y ⊆ g '' x}.ncard = {y ∈ facesOfDim P d | y ⊆ x}.ncard

name: EulersGem.ncard_sup_image
statement:
/-- A symmetry preserves the number of `d`-faces containing a set. -/
lemma ncard_sup_image (hg : g '' P = P) (d : ℤ) (x : Set R3) :
    {y ∈ facesOfDim P d | g '' x ⊆ y}.ncard = {y ∈ facesOfDim P d | x ⊆ y}.ncard

name: EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron.uniform
statement:
/-- **Flag-transitivity makes the incidence numbers uniform.** -/
theorem IsRegularPolyhedron.uniform {P : Set R3} (hP : IsRegularPolyhedron P)
    (hL : FaceLatticeFacts P) :
    ∃ s m, (∀ f ∈ facesOfDim P 2, {e ∈ facesOfDim P 1 | e ⊆ f}.ncard = s) ∧
      (∀ v ∈ facesOfDim P 0, {e ∈ facesOfDim P 1 | v ⊆ e}.ncard = m)

name: EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron.faceData
statement:
/-- **The combinatorial classification of regular polyhedra**, assuming only the general
face-lattice facts `FaceLatticeFacts`: the Schläfli type and the face counts are those of one
of the five Platonic solids. Euler's relation comes from the Euler–Poincaré root. -/
theorem IsRegularPolyhedron.faceData {P : Set R3} (hP : IsRegularPolyhedron P)
    (hL : FaceLatticeFacts P) :
    ∃ t ∈ platonicTypes, HasFaceData P t.2.2.1 t.2.2.2.1 t.2.2.2.2 t.1 t.2.1

name: EulersGem.simMap
statement:
/-- A similarity `x ↦ r • g x` as an injective affine map. -/
noncomputable def simMap (g : R3 ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] R3) (r : ℝ) : R3 →ᵃ[ℝ] R3 :=
  (LinearMap.lsmul ℝ R3 r).toAffineMap.comp g.toAffineEquiv.toAffineMap

name: EulersGem.simMap_apply
statement: lemma simMap_apply (g : R3 ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] R3) (r : ℝ) (x : R3) : simMap g r x = r • g x

name: EulersGem.simMap_injective
statement:
lemma simMap_injective (g : R3 ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] R3) {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) :
    Function.Injective (simMap g r)

name: EulersGem.Similar.ncard_facesOfDim
statement:
/-- Similar polyhedra have the same number of faces of each dimension. -/
theorem Similar.ncard_facesOfDim {P Q : Set R3} (h : Similar P Q) (d : ℤ) :
    (facesOfDim Q d).ncard = (facesOfDim P d).ncard

name: EulersGem.platonicSolid
statement:
/-- The five constructed solids, indexed: tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron,
icosahedron. -/
noncomputable def platonicSolid : Fin 5 → Set R3 :=
  ![Platonic3.tetrahedron, Platonic3.cube, Platonic3.octahedron, Platonic3.dodecahedron,
    Platonic3.icosahedron]

name: EulersGem.platonicSolid_vertices
statement:
lemma platonicSolid_vertices (i : Fin 5) :
    (facesOfDim (platonicSolid i) 0).ncard = ![4, 8, 6, 20, 12] i

name: EulersGem.platonic_not_similar
statement:
/-- **The five constructed solids are pairwise non-similar** (in both directions): they have
4, 8, 6, 20 and 12 vertices. -/
theorem platonic_not_similar {i j : Fin 5} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    ¬ Similar (platonicSolid i) (platonicSolid j)

name: EulersGem.platonicSolid_similar_unique
EulersGem.IsFlag
EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron
statement:
/-- **Regular convex polyhedron.** A three-dimensional convex polytope in `ℝ³` whose isometry
group is transitive on flags. -/
def IsRegularPolyhedron (P : Set R3) : Prop :=
  IsPolytope P ∧ affDim P = 3 ∧
    ∀ v e f v' e' f', IsFlag P v e f → IsFlag P v' e' f' →
      ∃ g : R3 ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] R3, g '' P = P ∧ g '' v = v' ∧ g '' e = e' ∧ g '' f = f'

name: EulersGem.Similar
EulersGem.eulerChar
statement:
/-- Euler characteristic of an `n`-simplex, including the empty face.

Index `c` runs over vertex-counts `0, …, n+1` (affine dimensions `-1, …, n`),
with sign `(-1)^c`. Matches Isabelle's `euler_char` for simplices. -/
def eulerChar (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  ∑ c ∈ range (n + 2), ((-1 : ℤ) ^ c) * ((n + 1).choose c : ℤ)

name: EulersGem.eulerChar_simplex
statement:
/-- **Main proved theorem (simplex case):** Euler characteristic of any `n`-simplex is `0`.

Corresponds to Isabelle `euler_0simplex_eq0` / `euler_nsimplex_eq0` and the binomial
identity `∑_{c=0}^{n+1} (-1)^c C(n+1,c) = 0` for `n+1 ≠ 0`. -/
theorem eulerChar_simplex (n : ℕ) : eulerChar n = 0

name: EulersGem.tetrahedron_polyhedron_numbers
statement:
/-- From face counts, the classical `V - E + F = 2` for a tetrahedron
(excluding empty face and the solid itself): `4 - 6 + 4 = 2`. -/
theorem tetrahedron_polyhedron_numbers :
    (faceCount 3 0 : ℤ) - faceCount 3 1 + faceCount 3 2 = 2

name: EulersGem.Simplex.body
statement:
/-- The geometric simplex spanned by an affine basis: the convex hull of its vertices. -/
def body (b : AffineBasis ι ℝ E) : Set E := convexHull ℝ (Set.range b)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.face
statement:
/-- The subsimplex spanned by a subset `S` of the vertices. -/
def face (b : AffineBasis ι ℝ E) (S : Finset ι) : Set E := convexHull ℝ (b '' ↑S)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.body_eq_convexHull_range
statement: lemma body_eq_convexHull_range : body b = convexHull ℝ (Set.range b)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.mem_body_iff
statement:
/-- Barycentric characterization of the simplex (Mathlib
`AffineBasis.convexHull_eq_nonneg_coord`). -/
lemma mem_body_iff {x : E} : x ∈ body b ↔ ∀ i, 0 ≤ b.coord i x

name: EulersGem.Simplex.coord_nonneg_of_mem_body
statement: lemma coord_nonneg_of_mem_body {x : E} (hx : x ∈ body b) (i : ι) : 0 ≤ b.coord i x

name: EulersGem.Simplex.convex_body
statement: lemma convex_body : Convex ℝ (body b)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.isPolytope_body
statement: lemma isPolytope_body : IsPolytope (body b)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.convex_face
statement: lemma convex_face (S : Finset ι) : Convex ℝ (face b S)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.face_subset_body
statement: lemma face_subset_body (S : Finset ι) : face b S ⊆ body b

name: EulersGem.Simplex.face_empty
statement: lemma face_empty : face b (∅ : Finset ι) = (∅ : Set E)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.coord_eq_zero_of_mem_face
EulersGem.Simplex.mem_face_of_coord_eq_zero
statement:
/-- Conversely, a point of the simplex whose coordinates outside `S` vanish lies in
`face b S`. -/
lemma mem_face_of_coord_eq_zero {S : Finset ι} {x : E} (hx : x ∈ body b)
    (h0 : ∀ i ∉ S, b.coord i x = 0) : x ∈ face b S

name: EulersGem.Simplex.mem_face_iff
statement:
lemma mem_face_iff {S : Finset ι} {x : E} (hx : x ∈ body b) :
    x ∈ face b S ↔ ∀ i ∉ S, b.coord i x = 0

name: EulersGem.Simplex.vertex_mem_face_iff
statement:
/-- A vertex lies in a subsimplex exactly when its index does. -/
lemma vertex_mem_face_iff {S : Finset ι} {i : ι} : b i ∈ face b S ↔ i ∈ S

name: EulersGem.Simplex.isFaceOf_face
statement:
/-- **The subsimplices are faces.** Extremeness is read off the barycentric coordinates:
a coordinate vanishing at an interior point of a segment, with both endpoints in the
simplex, must vanish at both endpoints. -/
theorem isFaceOf_face (S : Finset ι) : IsFaceOf (body b) (face b S)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.faceIdx
statement:
/-- The set of vertex indices lying in a given set. -/
noncomputable def faceIdx (F : Set E) : Finset ι :=
  open Classical in Finset.univ.filter fun i => b i ∈ F

name: EulersGem.Simplex.mem_faceIdx_iff
statement: lemma mem_faceIdx_iff {F : Set E} {i : ι} : i ∈ faceIdx b F ↔ b i ∈ F

name: EulersGem.Simplex.range_inter_eq_image_faceIdx
statement:
lemma range_inter_eq_image_faceIdx {F : Set E} :
    Set.range b ∩ F = b '' ↑(faceIdx b F)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.faces_eq_range_face
statement:
/-- The faces of a simplex are exactly the subsimplices. -/
theorem faces_eq_range_face :
    {F : Set E | IsFaceOf (body b) F} = Set.range (face b)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.face_subset_iff
statement: lemma face_subset_iff {S T : Finset ι} : face b S ⊆ face b T ↔ S ⊆ T

name: EulersGem.Simplex.face_injective
statement: lemma face_injective : Function.Injective (face b)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.affDim_face
statement:
/-- `affDim (face b S) = S.card - 1`: the subsimplex on `k` vertices has dimension `k−1`
(and the empty face has dimension `-1`). -/
theorem affDim_face (S : Finset ι) : affDim (face b S) = (S.card : ℤ) - 1

name: EulersGem.Simplex.facesOfDim_eq_image
statement:
/-- The `d`-faces of a simplex are the subsimplices on `d + 1` vertices. -/
theorem facesOfDim_eq_image (d : ℤ) :
    {F : Set E | IsFaceOf (body b) F ∧ affDim F = d} =
      face b '' {S : Finset ι | (S.card : ℤ) = d + 1}

name: EulersGem.Simplex.ncard_facesOfDim
statement:
/-- The number of `d`-faces of a simplex equals the number of `(d+1)`-element subsets of
the vertex index set. -/
theorem ncard_facesOfDim (d : ℤ) :
    {F : Set E | IsFaceOf (body b) F ∧ affDim F = d}.ncard =
      {S : Finset ι | (S.card : ℤ) = d + 1}.ncard

name: EulersGem.Simplex.body_eq_face_univ
statement: lemma body_eq_face_univ : body b = face b (Finset.univ : Finset ι)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.affDim_body
statement:
/-- A simplex on an affine basis is full-dimensional: `affDim = finrank`. -/
lemma affDim_body [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] :
    affDim (body b) = (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℤ)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.coordVec
statement:
/-- Riesz vector of the linear part of the `i`-th barycentric coordinate. -/
noncomputable def coordVec (i : ι) : E :=
  (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E).symm
    (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (b.coord i).linear)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.inner_coordVec
statement:
lemma inner_coordVec (i : ι) (x : E) :
    ⟪coordVec b i, x⟫ = (b.coord i).linear x

name: EulersGem.Simplex.coord_eq_inner_add
statement:
/-- Each barycentric coordinate is an inner product plus a constant. -/
lemma coord_eq_inner_add (i : ι) (x : E) :
    b.coord i x = ⟪coordVec b i, x⟫ + b.coord i 0

name: EulersGem.Simplex.coordHyperplane
statement:
/-- The hyperplane cutting out `0 ≤ b.coord i ·`. -/
noncomputable def coordHyperplane (i : ι) : Hyperplane E :=
  (-(coordVec b i), b.coord i 0)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.mem_coordHalfspace_iff
statement:
lemma mem_coordHalfspace_iff (i : ι) (x : E) :
    x ∈ closedHalfspace (coordHyperplane b i).1 (coordHyperplane b i).2 ↔
      0 ≤ b.coord i x

name: EulersGem.Simplex.coordHyperplanes
statement:
/-- The finite hyperplane arrangement of the barycentric coordinates. -/
noncomputable def coordHyperplanes : Set (Hyperplane E) := Set.range (coordHyperplane b)

name: EulersGem.Simplex.coordHyperplanes_finite
statement: lemma coordHyperplanes_finite : (coordHyperplanes b).Finite

name: EulersGem.Simplex.body_eq_iInter_closedHalfspace
statement:
/-- **H-representation of the simplex**: it is the intersection of the `Fintype.card ι`
closed halfspaces given by its barycentric coordinates. -/
theorem body_eq_iInter_closedHalfspace :
    body b = ⋂ h ∈ coordHyperplanes b, closedHalfspace h.1 h.2

name: EulersGem.Euler_Poincare_of_isPolytope
statement:
/-- A full-dimensional polytope in positive ambient dimension has Euler
characteristic one, without a supplied halfspace presentation. -/
theorem Euler_Poincare_of_isPolytope {p : Set E} (hp : IsPolytope p)
    (hdim : affDim p = Module.finrank ℝ E) (hn : 1 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ E) :
    faceEulerSum p (Module.finrank ℝ E) = 1

name: EulersGem.euler_relation_of_isPolytope
statement:
/-- Euler's relation for a convex polytope in a three-dimensional ambient
space, without a supplied halfspace presentation. -/
theorem euler_relation_of_isPolytope {p : Set E} (hp : IsPolytope p)
    (hdim : affDim p = 3) (hE : Module.finrank ℝ E = 3) :
    ({f : Set E | IsFaceOf p f ∧ affDim f = 0}.ncard : ℤ) -
      ({f : Set E | IsFaceOf p f ∧ affDim f = 1}.ncard : ℤ) +
      ({f : Set E | IsFaceOf p f ∧ affDim f = 2}.ncard : ℤ) = 2

name: EulersGem.euler_polyhedron
statement:
/-- Euler's polyhedron formula in real three-space. Its only geometric
hypotheses are a finite convex hull and affine dimension three. -/
theorem euler_polyhedron {p : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))}
    (hp : IsPolytope p) (hdim : affDim p = 3) :
    ({f : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) | IsFaceOf p f ∧ affDim f = 0}.ncard : ℤ) -
      ({f : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) | IsFaceOf p f ∧ affDim f = 1}.ncard : ℤ) +
      ({f : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) | IsFaceOf p f ∧ affDim f = 2}.ncard : ℤ) = 2

name: EulersGem.ZPhi
statement:
/-- `a + b φ`. -/
structure ZPhi where

  b : Int

name: EulersGem.instReprZPhi.repr
statement: deriving DecidableEq, Repr

statement: deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.instAdd
statement: instance : Add ZPhi := ⟨fun x y => ⟨x.a + y.a, x.b + y.b⟩⟩

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.instNeg
statement: instance : Neg ZPhi := ⟨fun x => ⟨-x.a, -x.b⟩⟩

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.instMul
statement:
/-- `(a + bφ)(c + dφ) = (ac + bd) + (ad + bc + bd)φ`, using `φ² = φ + 1`. -/
instance : Mul ZPhi := ⟨fun x y => ⟨x.a * y.a + x.b * y.b, x.a * y.b + x.b * y.a + x.b * y.b⟩⟩

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.zero_b

statement: @[simp] lemma one_a : (1 : ZPhi).a = 1

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.one_b
statement: @[simp] lemma one_b : (1 : ZPhi).b = 0

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.add_b

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.ofInt
statement:
/-- An integer. -/
def ofInt (n : Int) : ZPhi := ⟨n, 0⟩

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.toReal
statement:
/-- Evaluation at the golden ratio. -/
noncomputable def toReal (x : ZPhi) : ℝ := x.a + x.b * φ

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.toReal_zero
statement: @[simp] lemma toReal_zero : toReal 0 = 0

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.toReal_one
statement: @[simp] lemma toReal_one : toReal 1 = 1

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.toReal_ofInt
statement: @[simp] lemma toReal_ofInt (n : Int) : toReal (ofInt n) = n

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.toReal_add
statement: @[simp] lemma toReal_add (x y : ZPhi) : toReal (x + y) = toReal x + toReal y

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.toReal_neg
statement: @[simp] lemma toReal_neg (x : ZPhi) : toReal (-x) = -toReal x

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.toReal_sub
statement: @[simp] lemma toReal_sub (x y : ZPhi) : toReal (x - y) = toReal x - toReal y

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.toReal_mul
statement: @[simp] lemma toReal_mul (x y : ZPhi) : toReal (x * y) = toReal x * toReal y

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.sgnPQ
EulersGem.ZPhi.sgn
statement:
/-- The sign of `a + bφ`, computed with integers: `2(a + bφ) = (2a + b) + b√5`. -/
def sgn (x : ZPhi) : Int := sgnPQ (2 * x.a + x.b) x.b

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.two_toReal
statement:
lemma two_toReal (x : ZPhi) :
    2 * toReal x = ((2 * x.a + x.b : Int) : ℝ) + (x.b : ℝ) * √5

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.sgn_eq_one
statement:
/-- A computed sign `1` is a positive real. -/
lemma sgn_eq_one {x : ZPhi} (h : sgn x = 1) : 0 < toReal x

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.sgn_eq_neg_one
statement:
/-- A computed sign `-1` is a negative real. -/
lemma sgn_eq_neg_one {x : ZPhi} (h : sgn x = -1) : toReal x < 0

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.sgn_eq_zero
statement:
/-- A computed sign `0` is zero. -/
lemma sgn_eq_zero {x : ZPhi} (h : sgn x = 0) : toReal x = 0

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.sgn_nonneg
statement: lemma sgn_nonneg {x : ZPhi} (h0 : sgn x ≠ -1) (h2 : sgn x ≠ 2) : 0 ≤ toReal x

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.sgn_cases
statement: lemma sgn_cases (x : ZPhi) : sgn x = 0 ∨ sgn x = 1 ∨ sgn x = -1 ∨ sgn x = 2

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.toReal_eq_zero_iff_sgn
statement:
/-- A computed sign other than `0` (and not the error value) is a nonzero real. -/
lemma toReal_eq_zero_iff_sgn {x : ZPhi} (h2 : sgn x ≠ 2) : toReal x = 0 ↔ sgn x = 0

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V
statement:
/-- A vector in `ℤ[φ]³`. -/
structure V where
  x : ZPhi
  y : ZPhi
  z : ZPhi
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.instDecidableEqV.decEq
statement: deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.instReprV
statement: deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.instReprV.repr
statement: deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.instDecidableEqV
statement: deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.instAdd

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.instSub

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.instNeg

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.add_x

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.add_y

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.smul
statement:
/-- Scalar multiple. -/
def smul (c : ZPhi) (u : V) : V := ⟨c * u.x, c * u.y, c * u.z⟩

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.dot
statement:
/-- Dot product. -/
def dot (u v : V) : ZPhi := u.x * v.x + u.y * v.y + u.z * v.z

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.cross
EulersGem.ZPhi.V.toR3
statement:
/-- The real point. -/
noncomputable def toR3 (u : V) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) :=
  !₂[toReal u.x, toReal u.y, toReal u.z]

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.toR3_apply0

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.toR3_apply1

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.toR3_apply2

    (h2 : p 2 = q 2) : p = q

statement:
lemma inner_R3 (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    ⟪p, q⟫ = p 0 * q 0 + p 1 * q 1 + p 2 * q 2

statement: @[simp] lemma toR3_add (u v : V) : (u + v).toR3 = u.toR3 + v.toR3

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.toR3_sub
statement: @[simp] lemma toR3_sub (u v : V) : (u - v).toR3 = u.toR3 - v.toR3

statement: @[simp] lemma toR3_zero : (0 : V).toR3 = 0

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.toR3_smul
statement: @[simp] lemma toR3_smul (c : ZPhi) (u : V) : (smul c u).toR3 = toReal c • u.toR3

name: EulersGem.ZPhi.V.inner_toR3
statement: lemma inner_toR3 (u v : V) : ⟪u.toR3, v.toR3⟫ = toReal (dot u v)

name: Results.results_euler_characteristic
statement:
/-- **Euler characteristic.** A full-dimensional convex polytope, given as
the convex hull of finitely many points, has Euler–Poincaré characteristic `1`: the alternating sum of its
face counts, from vertices through the body, equals `1`. In dimension `3`
this is `V − E + F = 2`. -/
theorem results_euler_characteristic
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    {p : Set E}
    (hP : EulersGem.IsPolytope p)
    (hdim : EulersGem.affDim p = Module.finrank ℝ E)
    (hn : 1 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ E) :
    EulersGem.faceEulerSum p (Module.finrank ℝ E) = 1

name: Results.results_euler_relation_dimension_three
statement:
/-- **Euler's formula** (Euler's polyhedron formula; Paulson `Euler_relation`).
For a convex polytope in dimension 3, `V − E + F = 2`. Proved from the
Euler characteristic `1`: the only 3-face is the body itself, and removing
it from the alternating sum leaves `2`. -/
theorem results_euler_relation_dimension_three
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    {p : Set E}
    (hP : EulersGem.IsPolytope p)
    (hdim : EulersGem.affDim p = 3)
    (hE : Module.finrank ℝ E = 3) :
    ({f : Set E | EulersGem.IsFaceOf p f ∧ EulersGem.affDim f = 0}.ncard : ℤ) -
        ({f : Set E | EulersGem.IsFaceOf p f ∧ EulersGem.affDim f = 1}.ncard : ℤ) +
        ({f : Set E | EulersGem.IsFaceOf p f ∧ EulersGem.affDim f = 2}.ncard : ℤ) =
      2

name: Results.results_euler_polyhedron
statement:
/-- **Euler's polyhedron formula in real three-space.** The only geometric
hypotheses are that `p` is a finite convex hull and has affine dimension three. -/
theorem results_euler_polyhedron {p : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))}
    (hP : EulersGem.IsPolytope p) (hdim : EulersGem.affDim p = 3) :
    ({f : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) |
      EulersGem.IsFaceOf p f ∧ EulersGem.affDim f = 0}.ncard : ℤ) -
    ({f : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) |
      EulersGem.IsFaceOf p f ∧ EulersGem.affDim f = 1}.ncard : ℤ) +
    ({f : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) |
      EulersGem.IsFaceOf p f ∧ EulersGem.affDim f = 2}.ncard : ℤ) = 2

name: Results.results_pick_count_of_euler
statement:
/-- **Pick's count is Euler's formula for a triangulation.**
`A = T/2`, `V = I + B`, `F = T + 1`, `2E = 3T + B`, and `V − E + F = 2`
give `A = I + B/2 − 1`. The Euler input is not a bare hypothesis: a caller
passes `results_euler_relation_dimension_three` when those `(V, E, F)` are the
face counts of a convex 3-polytope, or the same numeral proved for a disk
triangulation. -/
theorem results_pick_count_of_euler
    (I B V E T F : ℕ) (A : ℚ)
    (hV : V = I + B)
    (hF : F = T + 1)
    (heuler : (V : ℤ) - E + F = 2)
    (hshake : 2 * E = 3 * T + B)
    (harea : A = (T : ℚ) / 2) :
    A = (I : ℚ) + (B : ℚ) / 2 - 1

name: Results.results_fan_pick_of_euler
statement:
/-- **Empty-fan Pick count, from the Euler characteristic.** A fan of an `n`-gon
has disk Euler number `2` because a triangle does (`triangle_disk_euler`, the
characteristic plus the exterior face) and each added vertex preserves it.
With area `T/2` and `I = 0`, that is `n/2 − 1`. -/
theorem results_fan_pick_of_euler (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
    ((n - 2 : ℕ) : ℚ) / 2 = (n : ℚ) / 2 - 1

name: Results.results_disk_pick_of_euler
statement:
/-- **Pick's count for a triangulated disk, from the characteristic.**
The corner cycle's Euler number is the fan's, which is the triangle's
characteristic plus the exterior face. Boundary insertions, diagonals, and
stellar subdivisions preserve it, so `V = I + B`, `T = 2I + B − 2` and area
`T/2` give `I + B/2 − 1`. -/
theorem results_disk_pick_of_euler
    (n B I : ℕ) (A : ℚ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnB : n ≤ B)
    (harea : A = ((2 * I + B - 2 : ℕ) : ℚ) / 2) :
    A = (I : ℚ) + (B : ℚ) / 2 - 1

name: Results.results_picks_of_empty_primitive_fan
statement:
/-- **Pick for an empty primitive polygon, from the characteristic.** The corner
fan is a primitive triangulation (`T = B − 2`). Its Euler number is the disk
Euler number, so the area is `B/2 − 1`. -/
theorem results_picks_of_empty_primitive_fan
    (P : EulersGem.Picks.LatticePolygon)
    (hverts : Function.Injective P.vertex)
    (hedge : EulersGem.Picks.LatticeFan.PrimitiveEdges P)
    (hsc : EulersGem.Picks.LatticeFan.StrictlyConvexCCW P)
    (hI : EulersGem.Picks.LatticeFan.EmptyInterior P) :
    MeasureTheory.volume P.convexHullRegion =
      ENNReal.ofReal ((P.B : ℚ) / 2 - 1)

name: Results.results_picks_theorem
statement:
/-- **Pick's theorem** for a strictly convex counterclockwise lattice polygon
with distinct vertices. The area is the Haar measure of the convex hull.
A primitive triangulation has `T = 2I + B − 2` triangles of shoelace `1/2`,
so the polygon shoelace is `T/2`. Those counts have disk Euler number `2`
by `triangulated_disk_euler_from_characteristic` (the triangle's
characteristic, kept by the fan and the later moves). `results_pick_count_of_euler`
turns `T/2` and that Euler number into `I + B/2 − 1`. -/
theorem results_picks_theorem
    (P : EulersGem.Picks.LatticePolygon) (S : Finset (ℤ × ℤ))
    (hS : (S : Set (ℤ × ℤ)) = P.interiorLatticePoints)
    (hverts : Function.Injective P.vertex)
    (hsc : EulersGem.Picks.LatticeFan.StrictlyConvexCCW P) :
    MeasureTheory.volume P.convexHullRegion =
      ENNReal.ofReal ((S.card : ℚ) + (P.B : ℚ) / 2 - 1)

name: Results.results_five_platonic_solids
statement:
/-- **Euler's formula leaves five Platonic solids.** A convex 3-polytope whose
faces are `s`-gons, with `m` faces at each vertex and two faces along each
edge, has `(s, m)` in the list below. The count `V − E + F = 2` in that
argument is `results_euler_relation_dimension_three`. The five pairs are the
tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron, with `(V, E, F)`
the solution of that formula together with the double-counting identities. -/
theorem results_five_platonic_solids :
    (∀ {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
        [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
        {p : Set E} {s m : ℕ},
        EulersGem.IsPolytope p →
        EulersGem.affDim p = 3 →
        Module.finrank ℝ E = 3 →
        3 ≤ s → 3 ≤ m →
        (∀ f ∈ EulersGem.Platonic.facesOfDim p 2,
          {e ∈ EulersGem.Platonic.facesOfDim p 1 | e ⊆ f}.ncard = s) →
        (∀ e ∈ EulersGem.Platonic.facesOfDim p 1,
          {f ∈ EulersGem.Platonic.facesOfDim p 2 | e ⊆ f}.ncard = 2) →
        (∀ v ∈ EulersGem.Platonic.facesOfDim p 0,
          {e ∈ EulersGem.Platonic.facesOfDim p 1 | v ⊆ e}.ncard = m) →
        (s, m) ∈ EulersGem.Platonic.schlafliPairs) ∧
      (EulersGem.Platonic.tetrahedron.V, EulersGem.Platonic.tetrahedron.E,
          EulersGem.Platonic.tetrahedron.F, EulersGem.Platonic.tetrahedron.s,
          EulersGem.Platonic.tetrahedron.m) = (4, 6, 4, 3, 3) ∧
      (EulersGem.Platonic.cube.V, EulersGem.Platonic.cube.E,
          EulersGem.Platonic.cube.F, EulersGem.Platonic.cube.s,
          EulersGem.Platonic.cube.m) = (8, 12, 6, 4, 3) ∧
      (EulersGem.Platonic.octahedron.V, EulersGem.Platonic.octahedron.E,
          EulersGem.Platonic.octahedron.F, EulersGem.Platonic.octahedron.s,
          EulersGem.Platonic.octahedron.m) = (6, 12, 8, 3, 4) ∧
      (EulersGem.Platonic.dodecahedron.V, EulersGem.Platonic.dodecahedron.E,
          EulersGem.Platonic.dodecahedron.F, EulersGem.Platonic.dodecahedron.s,
          EulersGem.Platonic.dodecahedron.m) = (20, 30, 12, 5, 3) ∧
      (EulersGem.Platonic.icosahedron.V, EulersGem.Platonic.icosahedron.E,
          EulersGem.Platonic.icosahedron.F, EulersGem.Platonic.icosahedron.s,
          EulersGem.Platonic.icosahedron.m) = (12, 30, 20, 3, 5)

name: Results.results_five_platonic_solids_constructed
statement:
/-- **The five Platonic solids exist.** The tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron and
icosahedron, each the convex hull of explicit points with coordinates in `ℤ[φ]`
(`φ = Real.goldenRatio`), are regular polyhedra — 3-dimensional convex polytopes whose
isometries act transitively on flags — with the classical vertex, edge and facet counts and
face type `{s, m}`. The face lattices are computed by the kernel (`decide +kernel`). -/
theorem results_five_platonic_solids_constructed :
    (EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron EulersGem.Platonic3.tetrahedron ∧
      EulersGem.Platonic3.HasFaceData EulersGem.Platonic3.tetrahedron 4 6 4 3 3) ∧
    (EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron EulersGem.Platonic3.cube ∧
      EulersGem.Platonic3.HasFaceData EulersGem.Platonic3.cube 8 12 6 4 3) ∧
    (EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron EulersGem.Platonic3.octahedron ∧
      EulersGem.Platonic3.HasFaceData EulersGem.Platonic3.octahedron 6 12 8 3 4) ∧
    (EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron EulersGem.Platonic3.dodecahedron ∧
      EulersGem.Platonic3.HasFaceData EulersGem.Platonic3.dodecahedron 20 30 12 5 3) ∧
    (EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron EulersGem.Platonic3.icosahedron ∧
      EulersGem.Platonic3.HasFaceData EulersGem.Platonic3.icosahedron 12 30 20 3 5)

name: Results.results_regular_polyhedron_face_data
statement:
/-- **The face data of a regular polyhedron — CONDITIONAL on `FaceLatticeFacts`.** A regular
polyhedron (flag-transitive convex 3-polytope in `ℝ³`) that satisfies the general
face-lattice facts `FaceLatticeFacts` has the counts `(V, E, F)` and type `{s, m}` of one of
the five Platonic solids. `FaceLatticeFacts` holds for every convex 3-polytope classically,
but that is **not proved** in this repository (it is the gap
`PlatonicGaps.GAP_faceLatticeFacts`); it is proved for the five constructed solids. This is
not uniqueness up to similarity. -/
theorem results_regular_polyhedron_face_data {P : Set EulersGem.R3}
    (hP : EulersGem.IsRegularPolyhedron P) (hL : EulersGem.FaceLatticeFacts P) :
    EulersGem.Platonic3.HasFaceData P 4 6 4 3 3 ∨
      EulersGem.Platonic3.HasFaceData P 8 12 6 4 3 ∨
      EulersGem.Platonic3.HasFaceData P 6 12 8 3 4 ∨
      EulersGem.Platonic3.HasFaceData P 20 30 12 5 3 ∨
      EulersGem.Platonic3.HasFaceData P 12 30 20 3 5

name: Results.results_platonic_solids_not_similar
statement:
/-- **The five constructed solids are pairwise non-similar** (they have 4, 8, 6, 20 and 12
vertices), so a polyhedron is similar to at most one of them. -/
theorem results_platonic_solids_not_similar {i j : Fin 5} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    ¬ EulersGem.Similar (EulersGem.platonicSolid i) (EulersGem.platonicSolid j)
